q: You made a mistake at work. Which thought helps you grow?
o: What can I learn from this for next time?
I should hide it so nobody knows.
e: A growth mindset turns a mistake into a lesson - “What now?” instead of “Why me?”.

q: Feeling angry is…
o: a natural emotion - what matters is how you respond
a sign you are a bad person
something to hide at all costs
e: Gussa aana galat nahi hai - gusse mein kiya gaya reaction relationships ko affect kar sakta hai.

q: Before reacting in anger, the most helpful first step is to…
o: say everything you feel at once
pause and take a slow breath
walk away and never discuss it
e: A pause creates choice. Slow breaths first, then respond.

q: Which of these is naming your emotion?
o: I feel hurt and a little ignored right now.
e: Naming the feeling - hurt, ignored - is the first step of emotional awareness.

q: Rest is…
e: Rest is not giving up. It's how you restore yourself.

q: Saying “no” to a request means…
o: you are including yourself in the care you give everyone else
e: Saying no doesn't make you selfish. Aapka “nahi” bhi ek mindful decision hai.

q: Someone hasn't replied to your message for a few hours. The calmest thought is…
o: They must be angry with me.
They might be busy - I'll give them space.
I'll keep messaging until they reply.
e: Not every silence is rejection. Give people space - and give yourself peace.

q: Which statement shows self-compassion?
o: I should have known better, I'm so stupid.
I did the best I could with what I knew then.
Others have it worse, so I can't feel bad.
e: Self-compassion is speaking to yourself the way you would to a dear friend.

q: Strong women…
e: Strong rehna achha hai, lekin har waqt strong rehna zaroori nahi hai.

q: A boundary is…
o: a doorway that tells people how to love you well
e: A boundary is not a punishment. It tells people how to love you well.

q: Emotional awareness means…
o: noticing and understanding what you feel
e: The goal is emotional awareness, not emotional suppression.

q: Feeling irritated while managing home and office every day may mean…
o: you may be emotionally exhausted and need support
e: Irritation is often a sign of exhaustion - a signal to ask for support, not to push harder.

q: You keep saying “no” but still accept the same behaviour. What usually happens?
o: The other person may never understand your boundary is real
e: Your “no” becomes powerful when your actions support it.

q: A healthy way to express hurt is…
o: saying calmly, “I felt hurt when this happened”
e: Express hurt calmly, instead of going silent or exploding.

q: Your honest words upset a friend. Whose job is it to manage their feelings?
o: Theirs - your job is to say it kindly
e: Say the true thing kindly, then let it land where it lands.

q: Which is a sign you may be someone's backup plan?
o: You are always the one adjusting and waiting
e: Look at patterns, not promises. If you are always adjusting, you are carrying it alone.

q: Leaving a relationship that keeps hurting you is…
e: Leaving is not failing. Staying is not loyalty.

q: Some people come into our lives as…
e: Har rishta nibhane ke liye nahi hota. Kuch sirf kuch sikhane ke liye aate hain.

q: If someone does not respect you, the healthiest step is to…
o: set boundaries and protect your peace
e: You can't make someone respect you. Choose yourself, and protect your peace.

q: Silence in a relationship…
o: can mean tiredness, stress or needing space
e: Don't fill silence with assumptions - ask calmly if it matters.

q: Starting with “I feel…” instead of “You always…” helps because it…
e: “I” statements open a conversation; “you always” starts a fight.

q: Missing someone you left is…
o: not, by itself, a reason to go back
e: Missing someone is not a reason to go back.

q: Loneliness can make an old situation look…
e: Loneliness will make an old situation look softer than it was.

q: To ask for what you need in a relationship, start with…
e: One calm sentence, without a long explanation, is enough.

q: A limiting belief is…
o: a fact about who you are
an old idea that quietly decides what you think you are allowed to do
e: Limiting beliefs are learned - so they can be questioned and changed.

q: The rules you agreed to when you knew less…
o: can be changed - you know more now
e: You are allowed to change the rules. You know more now; you can choose again.

q: Change often feels like ___ before it feels like freedom.
e: Change can feel like loss before it feels like freedom.

q: “Why me?” keeps you stuck. Which question moves you forward?
e: Shift the question, shift your perspective, shift your next step.

q: Healing means…
o: learning when it's safe to let go of old protection
e: Healing is learning when it's safe to let go.

q: What happened to you is…
o: part of your story, not the definition of you
e: You are not the worst thing that was done to you.

q: Progress is…
e: Progress is not the absence of the wound. It is a shorter walk home.

q: Waiting to feel completely certain before acting often…
o: keeps good plans stuck in the drafts folder
e: Waiting to feel certain is how good lives stay in the drafts folder.

q: The version of you that you want is built…
e: It is not built in one dramatic weekend - it is built in unremarkable, repeated days.

q: Gratitude and ambition are…
o: able to live together without apology
e: You can hold both without apologising for either.

q: You cannot heal in an environment that…
e: You cannot heal in the same environment that keeps reopening the wound.

q: Stop shrinking to fit rooms you have…
e: Stop shrinking to fit rooms you have already outgrown.

q: Your teenage child ignores your reminders to study. Which response protects the relationship?
o: “I care about your studies. Let's make a realistic timetable together.”
e: Pause, find the real concern, and communicate without insults or threats.

q: A relative keeps calling you at midnight. A clear boundary sounds like…
o: “I can't take calls after 9 pm - let's talk in the morning.”
e: One calm sentence, then act on it the same way every time.

q: You compare yourself with a friend's “perfect” Instagram life and feel low. A helpful thought is…
o: Social media shows highlights - my journey is my own.
e: Comparison measures your inside against someone else's outside.

q: A colleague takes credit for your idea. The most effective first step is to…
o: speak to them calmly and state what happened
e: Respond, don't react: calm, direct and specific.

q: You said yes to too many things and now feel resentful. Next time you can…
o: pause before agreeing and check your time and energy
cancel everything at the last minute
e: A pause before “yes” protects both your energy and your relationships.

q: Your partner forgets a date that matters to you. Which response builds the relationship?
o: “I felt hurt it was forgotten - it matters to me.”
e: Say what you felt and why it matters - without attacking.

q: After a setback, the most useful thing to do within 24 hours is…
o: one small action that moves you forward
e: Small, doable actions rebuild a sense of control faster than waiting to feel ready.

q: You catch yourself thinking, “Main sabke liye kar rahi hoon - but mere liye kaun?” A healthy response is to…
o: make a little time for yourself - that is self-respect too
e: Apne liye time nikalna bhi self-respect hai.

q: Someone calls your boundary “selfish”. The best response is to…
o: stay kind and consistent - their discomfort doesn't make you wrong
e: Some people get upset at first, especially those who benefited from you having none.

q: You feel a strong emotion but can't name it. A good first step is to…
o: notice where you feel it in your body and breathe
e: Your body often notices before your mind does. Start there.

q: A friend shares her worries with you. Listening well means…
o: planning your reply while she talks
listening to understand, and asking a question
changing the topic to your problems
e: Listen to understand, not just to reply.

q: Every morning you check everyone's messages before anything else. A mindful change could be…
o: pausing to check in with yourself before your phone
e: Start the day answering to yourself before you answer to anyone else.

q: Coaching is different from therapy because coaching…
o: works on your present patterns and what you can do next
e: Coaching focuses on what is happening now and what you can do differently.

q: When might coaching NOT be the right help?
o: When you want to set goals
When clinical or therapeutic support is needed
e: Har problem ka solution coaching nahi hota - aur sahi help lena weakness nahi, wisdom hai.

q: Fear can protect you from getting hurt - and it can also…
o: protect you from being truly alive
e: You don't have to keep carrying the armor that once helped you survive.

q: A self-respecting response to repeated disrespect is…
o: knowing your worth and protecting your peace
e: Set boundaries. Protect your peace. Know your worth.

q: Most stuck decisions are not unclear. They are…
e: Often you already know - the hard part is the cost of choosing.

q: Keeping everyone comfortable by disappearing yourself is…
e: Disappearing to keep the peace is not harmony. It is a quiet form of absence.

q: Effort is not always the missing ingredient. Sometimes…
e: Some things don't grow because of where they are planted, not how hard you try.

q: You keep trying to guarantee an outcome. The truth is…
o: a guarantee was never on offer - you choose your effort and response
e: You keep trying to guarantee the outcome. That was never on offer.

q: Healthy love feels like…
o: safety, respect and being able to be yourself
having to prove yourself every day
e: In healthy love you don't have to audition for your place.

q: Not every healthy relationship is…
e: Healthy doesn't mean perfect - it means repair is possible.

q: Being proud of the woman who kept going is…
o: giving yourself the credit you deserve
e: Aapne sirf survive nahi kiya - aapne khud ko sambhala, seekha aur grow kiya.

q: “Jab aap khud ko samajhne lagti hain…”
o: you start responding to life differently
e: Understanding yourself changes how you respond - and that changes everything around it.
